discovery: Theoretical prediction and establishment of altermagnetism as a third fundamental class of collinear magnetic order

nominees.name: Tomáš Jungwirth
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague; University of Nottingham

nominees.name: Libor Šmejkal
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Dresden; Institute of Physics, Czech Academy of Sciences

motivation: For seventy years collinear magnets were classified as ferromagnets or antiferromagnets. Using spin-group symmetry analysis, Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth showed that a third, symmetry-distinct phase exists: altermagnets. In these materials the compensated sublattices are related by rotations rather than translations or inversion, producing zero net magnetization yet large, momentum-dependent, non-relativistic spin splitting of d-, g- or i-wave character. They predicted concrete candidates (RuO2, MnTe, CrSb and others) together with signatures including the anomalous Hall effect and spin-split bands. Between 2023 and 2025 these predictions were confirmed by spin- and angle-resolved photoemission and by X-ray magnetic circular dichroism imaging of altermagnetic domains. This is a general organizing principle derived from symmetry, validated experimentally across many materials. It opens a new route to fast, stray-field-free spintronics and offers a fresh setting for unconventional superconductivity and intertwined orders.
